# Task: make a bare `bee herding run` resolve its agent from the configured tier slot

You are a standalone coding agent. IGNORE any repo workflow/skill system you may notice
(`.bee/`, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md rituals) — do not run workflow commands, do not claim or cap
anything, do not read skills. Just do the code change below, run the test, commit, and report.

## Where

Repo (your cwd, a git worktree on branch `wt/herding-bare-agent`):
`/home/thanhsmind/projects/goglbe/beehive--wt--herding-bare-agent`

Edit exactly ONE file:
`packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/wave.rs`

Do NOT touch `herding/run.rs` or `herding/control_loop.rs` — other work is live in those files.

## The problem

`.bee/config.json` holds two independent places naming which external agent a herded worker runs as:

1. `models.claude.generation = {"kind":"herding","agent":"agy-flash","fallback":"default"}`
   — the cell-execution tier slot. Only the dispatch/model-guard path reads it today.
2. `herding.agent_command = "claude-sonnet"` — the default `resolve_agent_command` uses when no
   agent name is passed.

So the user configured `agy-flash` and a bare `bee herding run` opened `claude-sonnet`.
The tier slot is where the role→agent mapping is configured; the pane-opening verb must obey it.

## The change (locked decisions D1–D5)

In `resolve_agent_command(cfg: &Value, agent: Option<&str>) -> Result<(String, Vec<String>, BTreeMap<String, String>), AgentCommandError>`:

Insert ONE new step between the explicit-name lookup and the `herding.agent_command` lookup.
Final precedence:

1. `agent = Some(name)` — unchanged, resolved through `resolve_from_registry`.
2. **NEW** — the cell-execution tier slot: `cfg["models"][<runtime>]["generation"]`, but ONLY when
   it is an object with `kind == "herding"` AND an `agent` field that is a non-empty string.
   Resolve that name through `resolve_from_registry` — the exact same path step 1 takes.
3. `herding.agent_command` as a plain string — unchanged.
4. the array split / built-in default — unchanged.

Rules that must hold:

- **Slot shape (D2).** Only `{"kind":"herding","agent":"<non-empty string>"}` participates.
  `{"kind":"herding"}` with no agent, a plain model-name string like `"sonnet"`, `{"kind":"cli",…}`,
  `null`, absent, or a non-object — every one of these is SKIPPED and resolution falls through to
  step 3 exactly as it does today. An `agent` present but empty/whitespace-only is also skipped.
- **Runtime (D3).** `<runtime>` is the `BEE_RUNTIME` env var when it names one of
  `claude` / `codex` / `opencode`, else `claude`. This mirrors the unknown-runtime fallback in
  `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/models.rs` (`resolve_tier`, ~line 327).
  Add NO new CLI flag and change NO call site. Prefer a pure helper that takes the runtime name as
  a parameter, with a thin env-reading wrapper — so tests never have to mutate process env.
- **Fail closed (D4).** A slot naming an agent that is not in the `herding.agents` registry must
  return `AgentCommandError::UnknownAgent` listing every known key — exactly like a bad `--agent`.
  It must NEVER silently fall through to `herding.agent_command`. Silent-wrong-agent is the bug
  being fixed.
- **Env map.** The function returns a triple `(kind, args, env)`. The registry entry's `env` map
  must come through the new branch INTACT, exactly as the `--agent` path returns it. Do not return
  an empty map on the slot path.
- **Doc comment.** The function's doc comment currently enumerates the three reference spellings
  (herd-registry D2). Extend that enumeration so it names the new slot step in its precedence
  position. Keep the existing comment voice.
- `bee herding wave` calls `resolve_agent_command(cfg, None)` and inherits the new step for free —
  that is intended (D5). No change needed there.

`cfg` is already the WHOLE `.bee/config.json` document, so `models` is in hand. No new plumbing.

## Tests (add beside the existing resolver tests in the same file)

Cover, at minimum:

a. the slot wins over a differing `herding.agent_command`;
b. an explicit agent name still wins over the slot;
c. each of: kind-herding-with-no-agent, a plain model-name slot, a `kind:"cli"` slot — falls
   through to `agent_command` unchanged;
d. a slot naming an agent absent from `herding.agents` returns `UnknownAgent` (not the
   `agent_command` value);
e. a slot resolving to an object-shaped registry entry (`{"argv":[…],"env":{…}}`) carries that
   entry's `env` through;
f. an unknown/absent runtime name reads the `claude` block.

workers.task:
Find and fix one bug in `bee herding run`'s brief-pointer delivery, in the checkout at /home/thanhsmind/projects/goglbe/beehive--wt--herding-pointer-delivery (branch wt/herding-pointer-delivery). Work only there.

## The live incident (evidence, all real)

Two `bee herding run` jobs were spawned in parallel from the same orchestrator session, seconds apart:
- job "bhv-1-r1" — pane w4:p1D — pointer delivered fine, agent worked normally.
- job "bee-bin-refresh" — pane w4:p1E — the round-1 pointer NEVER reached the agent. The pane sat at the Antigravity CLI (agy) boot banner with the spawn keystrokes visibly ECHOED ABOVE the banner (text "agy --dangerouslagy --danger ously-permissions -skip-permissions" scrambled/duplicated in the scrollback — the start command's keystrokes interleaved and re-echoed), an empty prompt, agent state "idle", and .bee/mailbox/bee-bin-refresh/log.txt EMPTY. No result was ever written until a human manually sent the pointer text to the pane ~5 minutes later, after which the job completed normally.
- The pane runs agy (kind "agy" in job.json); the agy CLI had just self-updated ("Update installed" appeared), so its boot was slower than usual.
- The orchestrator's `bee herding run` invocation for bee-bin-refresh did NOT fail fast: it kept waiting (idle-timeout 1200, ceiling 3600) with no visible re-send that reached the agent.

## Your job

1. Read the delivery path in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs: the ready-wait before the send, the pointer send, the bounded re-sends, and the delivery receipt ("a state transition the agent itself caused" — agent state moving to working/done or the result file appearing). Also read skills/bee-herding/references/spawn-proof.md and docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/handing-a-foreign-agent-its-brief.md for the intended contract.
2. Reconstruct how this incident fits the code: the scrambled double echo of the start command suggests keystrokes were sent while the shell/agent was not ready, or sent twice interleaved (two parallel runs sharing something — a pane targeting race, a readiness check that read the WRONG pane, or readiness satisfied by the shell rather than the agent). Find the concrete defect — the code path where a parallel second spawn can pass the ready gate or the receipt check without the agent ever receiving the pointer, or where the bounded re-send loop can conclude without a real receipt while the run keeps waiting to timeout anyway.
3. Name the root cause precisely (file:line) in your result. If the evidence supports several candidate defects, fix the one the evidence proves and list the others as findings.
4. Fix it in run.rs (and its test module). The fix must keep the existing contracts: pointer over one line, bounded re-sends, receipt = agent-caused state transition, typed failure when attempts run out (never silent waiting to ceiling with an undelivered brief — that is exactly what happened here).
5. Add/extend unit tests in the existing run.rs test style covering the failure mode you found (e.g. a receipt check that would have passed/waited wrongly under this incident's sequence now fails typed / resends correctly).

Prove it: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- herding:: — green, from the checkout root.

Commit ALL changes as ONE commit, imperative subject, body's last line exactly:
cell: hpd-1

Result JSON: summary = root cause in one line + fix in one line; files_changed; proof = the test command and its tail line; add a "findings" array line for any additional suspect you did not fix.
